summary:
The build brief (c62h-bound-brief.md, 540 lines, sha256 ba6bdeb0...) faithfully carries Mustafa's C62H-BOUND-YES, my C5-C11, my r2 rulings and the test-engineer's ten points. Nothing in it rewords a frozen text. It can be built once three Medium wording fixes are made and B-1 to B-3 are ruled as below. I only read; the one file I wrote is my notes file (advisor-c62h-bound-brief.md).

What I checked myself:
- Hashes. I recomputed texts v3 (3f21c9b7), the freeze (9cb8be17), the paste (cfac7502), the runners (u4r-run.sh e9437ae2, main-run.sh 8df2dee3, peak.py dfacdcc0, c-u4r-runs.mjs 99dd070e) and the three base files (marks.json 9fb5be57, SERIES.md 3411eee7, README.md b49f3441). All equal the brief's values. Base 442a284 has spike tree 6ca9f77f, the same as today's head. Between 717b802 and 442a284 the only spike change is b5cb253's raw-logs.sha256.
- The frozen texts go in by script only. I ran the brief's insert algorithm in memory, writing no file, and got all four expected 'after' hashes exactly: SERIES.md part 1 89295b57, SERIES.md part 3 6898e119, marks.json c1935a5b, README.md f3c3c804.
  - marks.json still parses; its diff is +26 -0.
  - README's refill is 16 lines, none over 120 columns. Its word diff is one insert of 73 words: the frozen sentence.
  - The insert script checks texts v3, the freeze and every block by sha256 before it writes, and the built check re-checks them before the re-judge and before each set. Every change after his yes goes back to him (brief :137-139, :351-352, :515).
- Coverage, item by item, all present:
  - C5: JDG-ONLY-1 is out (:68-71).
  - C6: the runner change (:273-291).
  - C7: groups on a slot with no session are an error (:159).
  - C8: the :320 row goes in by script.
  - C9: the freeze and the built check (:87-139).
  - C10: the runner sha256s, the stop counts 30 / 24 / 23 and the judge peaks as projections.
  - C11: the order, the readers at xhigh, the 13:35 read line, and the (c) lines kept until both sets PASS, B1's until U4g (:335-353, :491-499).
  - TE-CB-1 to -10 and TE-cond-6.
  - other_changes 6, all eight items.
  - His words: the freeze, the P0 re-judge with the same-answers comparison (:375-406), the 1,050 stop and the stop rules.
- Code citations: about 40 spot-checked; all hold.
- B-2's claims hold on the fixtures. base and lost-group change answers as stated unless edited, and hashed-and-incomplete moves from INVALID to FAIL (A 1). none-compared reads A 6 and stays FAIL. All other -17 L1 cases keep their answers, and the L2 cases are untouched.
- The re-judge comparison fits the real P0 verdict files. A part with no runs lists no checks. The new planted bug adds exactly one bites entry and one 'no run yet' line to each file.

Order: build, then the review round, then the merge and the head check, then the P0 re-judge, then P2, then P3, then the report. Running the re-judge before the sets is right. His words say only 'after the build'. It is one cheap judge pass on old logs, and a changed answer then stops the lane before 46 minutes of runs.

Rulings on the brief's questions:
- B-1, yes. Commit 1 carries the SERIES row and the (18) to (19) header change by the script's part 1; the lab's contract test needs them (contract.rs:502-513). No text changes.
- B-2, in, in commit 3, with condition 5. These edits are a consequence of the frozen texts, not a new decision: texts v3's readme-placement block says 'this contract change ships together with npt-judge and its fixtures'. The lane stays within the planned size: about 690 lines against a range of 545 to 755, and the stop at 1,050.
- B-3, confirmed: the kept P0 set is 93509dfd7fd1 (advisor-brawl1-sets-p0-full.md:7; advisor-u4r-sets-r2-full.md:10).

What I could not check: I built and ran nothing in this read-only seat. The check.mjs counts, the planted bugs, and the judged 0/0 and 48/48 results are still to be shown by the build and the runs.

findings.where: Brief :39-51 ("one, by either route"; route W "at each step's end it stops, and the main session commits that step"; "The main session runs the insert script on the worktree"), :209-210 (B-1: without part 1, contract r2 fails). Sources: C11 (advisor-c62h-bound-full.json, conditions: "by the main session or in one isolated worktree"); card .checkpoints/netcode-proof-test.md:92 ("its build from this head in its own worktree"); brawl1-brief.md:12-13 and :208-216 (one builder, uncommitted diff, merged once).
findings.fix:
Name one route. Recommended: W, the card's plan and BRAWL-1's precedent. Write its mechanics:
- One agent launch per commit step: general-purpose, opus, effort xhigh, no isolation, told the worktree path.
- Each launch ends at a clean point after its step's check.mjs, plants and SIZE-CHECK, with the step's files staged. The main session commits that step in the worktree before the next launch.
- The main session runs the insert script's part 1 in the worktree before step 1's launch, and part 3 plus the built check before step 3's launch. That launch does B-2's fixture files and check.mjs.
- A fix pass is one more launch.
If route M is chosen instead, delete route W's lines.

findings.where: Brief :304-308 (SIZE-CHECK `git diff --numstat <LANE_BASE> -- spikes/netcode-proof/`), :486 (report: "SIZE-CHECK per step and in total"), :405 and :444-445 (the re-judge's and the sets' results are committed under spikes/netcode-proof/results/). Sources: history.md:2173 ("the build stops and tells me past 1,050"); c62h-bound-paste.md:87 (evidence harnesses are not counted) and :89 (the stop line's command); results/u4r/93509dfd7fd1/P0/verdict.json is 698 lines, verdict-bites.json 356, and each P2/P3 verdict.json 680.
findings.what: After the re-judge and the two sets are committed, the same command would count about 3,000 lines of verdicts and runs.txt. A total taken for the report would then pass 1,050 and trigger his stop falsely, or leave the builder to decide on an exclusion himself. The fix pass's commit is also not named as a SIZE-CHECK point.
findings.fix: SIZE-CHECK reads `git diff --numstat <LANE_BASE> <step> -- spikes/netcode-proof/ ':(exclude)spikes/netcode-proof/results'`. It runs after each commit, the fix pass included. The total is the figure at the last code commit (commit 4 or the fix pass), stated as such in the report. Committed verdicts and runs.txt are evidence: named in the report, not counted, as the paste says of evidence.

findings.where: Brief :509-517 ("His (they stand ...)" stop rules). Sources: c62h-bound-paste.md:120-124 (the post's three stop rules), adopted by history.md:2175 ("The stop rules of your post stand. The check is never reworded to fit."); the size stop at history.md:2173 and paste :89.
findings.what:
The section headed 'His' rewords the post's rules instead of quoting them.
- Bullet 3 drops the post's comma ('48 on its own check, with every other check passing and no gap') and adds clauses. It can then be read as stopping only when every other check passes and there is no gap, so a planted-bug run reading 48 with a gap, or with the other figure failing, would go to the advisor instead of to Mustafa.
- Bullet 1 adds 'measured'.
Under the natural reading the substance is not loosened, and section 8.4's expected lines still catch every deviation. But rules he adopted should stand word for word.
findings.fix:
Quote the post's three stop rules word for word (paste :120-124) and the size line (paste :89). Under them, list the brief's working reading as the advisor's reading:
- measured scope (paste :106: outside the measured ten minutes 'no lost tick is checked, as the wording says');
- r2 TE-cond-6 for planted bugs: the run is valid; its own figure reads exactly 48 (fail); the other new figure and mismatches read 0 (pass); gaps are empty; the lab's N equals the judge's figure A.
Any other reading on a planted-bug run goes to Mustafa.

findings.where: Brief :389-404 (two judge calls; "(ii) at most one -17 why line"). Sources: history.md:2174 ("a judge call, no new runs"); c-u4r-runs.mjs:35-41 (U4r-F2: one call over the whole P0 folder projected over the 10 GiB line); results/u4r/93509dfd7fd1/P0/verdict.json and verdict-bites.json (-17's why lines and bites list).
findings.what: His words say 'a judge call'. The brief makes the set's two calls, measured/ then bites/. That is right in substance, but the report does not say why. Separately, the comparison allows 'at most one' new why line, where exactly one is expected in each file.
findings.fix: The report line says the re-judge is the kept set's two judge calls, as that set was judged (U4r-F2's memory split), with no new runs. The comparison asserts exactly one removed why line, `bite PM-0001-17/link-lost-overstated: no run yet`, in each file.

findings.where: Brief :257-269 (B-2) and :491-493 (the 13:35 read line). Sources: history.md:2129 (13:35 rule: a reviewer's read of every judge change, named in its own report line); history.md:2174 ("A changed judge must give the same answers on a set it was not changed for"); crates/judge/tests/fixtures.rs:392-418, :226-249.
findings.what: B-2 changes an existing fixture's expected answer: hashed-and-incomplete goes from INVALID to FAIL. The report does not yet have to name that, or show that no other judge test's assertion moved.

findings.where: Brief :286-288 (the dry-print harness 'asserts' 'about 552 MiB' and 'about 1,530 MiB'), :469 ('L about 2 % of S'). Source: c-u4r-runs.mjs:212-250 (runBytes, judgeRoom); computed with the runner's figures: P2 bites 106.8 MiB giving 552, P3 524.4 MiB giving 1530, P2 measured 780.8 MiB giving 2129.
findings.what: A script cannot assert 'about'; the builder would have to pick a tolerance. The runner's printed figures are exact.
findings.fix: Assert the exact printed values: P2 measured 2129, P2 bites 552, P3 1530; B1 2253 if B1's judge line is shown. Make 'L about 2 % of S' a value that is reported, not a pass bar; the bar there is B 0 and the identities.

findings.where: Brief, whole (no risk-tier line). Source: main's .claude/agents/advisor.md, Plan review checklist ('The risk tier is named').
findings.what: The brief names no risk tier.
findings.fix: Add one line: risk tier 1 (spike code, its tests and marks under spikes/netcode-proof/, on PR #40). Its reviewers are the round's three; no tier-2 path is touched.

conditions: 1. ADV-CBB-1: name one route in the brief, and write that route's mechanics: launches, commits, and when the insert script's parts 1 and 3 and the built check run. Recommended: route W, one agent launch per commit step.
2. ADV-CBB-2: SIZE-CHECK excludes spikes/netcode-proof/results/ and also runs after the fix pass. The total is the figure at the last code commit.

3. ADV-CBB-3: section 10 quotes the post's three stop rules and the size line word for word (c62h-bound-paste.md:120-124, :89). The brief's working reading follows as the advisor's reading: measured scope, and r2 TE-cond-6's planted-bug criteria. Any other reading on a planted-bug run goes to Mustafa.
4. B-1 ruled yes, as written: commit 1 carries the insert script's part 1. The expected SERIES.md after part 1 is 89295b57..., which I reproduced.

5. B-2 ruled in, in commit 3: four files, about 40 lines.
- The lines count in SIZE-CHECK, and the size line in the report names the four files beyond the paste's table.
- The test-engineer's 13:35 read covers fixtures.rs and the fixture files.
- The report names hashed-and-incomplete's move from INVALID to FAIL as the only changed fixture answer (ADV-CBB-5).
- No other existing test's assertion is edited. Any other changed answer stops for the advisor.
6. B-3 confirmed: the kept P0 set is 93509dfd7fd1. Both P0 folders stay unpacked until the report has reached Mustafa, and the report names this reading.
7. Apply ADV-CBB-4, -6 and -7 in the same revision of the brief.
8. The order stands as written: the P0 re-judge comes after the pushed head's check and before P2; a changed answer stops the lane before the sets.

9. The main session checks the revised brief against conditions 1-7: a word diff against ba6bdeb0..., shown in the notes, touching only these points. The new sha256 goes on the card before the build starts. No new advisor run is needed unless a condition is applied differently from this text.
